newsitem.title: USA: DuPont sees no charges from alliance.
newsitem.headline: DuPont sees no charges from alliance.

text.p: DuPont Co's information technology alliance with Andersen Consulting and Computer Sciences Corp will not require any extraordinary expenses or charges, DuPont chief information officer Cinda Hallman said on Wednesday.

Speaking to reporters in a late-afternoon telephone news conference, Hallman said "the time frame is for (the alliance) to be operational by the second quarter of 1997," including the transfer of DuPont workers to the two alliance partners.
DuPont Co said earlier Wednesday it agreed to form technology and consulting alliances with Computer Sciences and Andersen, expected to be worth more than $4 billion over 10 years.

The nation's largest chemical company said that assuming final agreements are reached, about 2,600 employees will be offered jobs with Computer Sciences and about 500 would be offered jobs with Andersen, while DuPont will retain 1,100 of the 4,200 employees in its information systems operation.
Hallman said the DuPont workers to be offered jobs at Computer Sciences and Andersen will remain in the Wilmington, Del. area and will be offered "comparable" compensation and benefits.
Hallman declined to elaborate on how the 10-year $4 billion contracts would be divided between the two companies, except to note how many employees each of the partners will add on.
She said the contracts were "expected to materialize into five to 10 percent cost improvements over time."
Hallman said the deal was different from traditional outsourcing because "DuPont was maintaining the role of leader and manager."
Hallman said there were no current plans to move other DuPont information technology staff as a result of the deal.
